title: Morphology and Carbon Isotope Composition of Placer Diamonds from the Northeastern Siberian Platform
content: The relationship between the morphology and the isotopic composition of carbon (δ¹³C) of placer diamonds from the northeast of the Siberian Platform was investigated in order to identify genetic differences between mineral varieties according to Y. L. Orlov’s clas-sification. Diamonds from the Bulkur, Ebelyakh, Kholomolookh, Mayat, and Morgogor placers were studied. 110 author’s δ¹³C determinations were compared with published data, including local SIMS analyses (the combined set of samples consists of 249 crys-tals). Differences in the distribution of the isotopic composition of carbon have been identified: octahedra and dodecahedroids of variety  I are characterized by predomi-nantly mantle‑like δ¹³C values; cuboids of variety II have a wide isotopic range, while the studied cuboids of  III variety and diamonds of varieties V–VII are characterized by predominantly isotopically light carbon. It has been exhibited that widespread natural dissolution caused significant alteration of the initial growth forms of crystals and can lead to morphological convergence of various mineralogical varieties, making their di-agnosis more difficult. The identified patterns are consistent with the hypothesis of polygenetic and multi‑stage diamond formation under the conditions of mantle envi-ronment evolution and the possible involvement of recycled carbon. It is assumed that the observed relationship between morphology and δ¹³C reflects a combination of het-erogeneity of diamond populations and the final processes of natural dissolution associ-ated with the conditions of being in a fluid‑saturated melt that transported the dia-monds to the Earth’s crust.
